feature.summary: One generated catalog of models, providers, provider routes, capabilities, plan tiers, aliases and lifecycle (stage, deprecation, retirement). A developer edits curated JSON and runs the sync command. Web, Mobile, the extensions and the server read the compiled output through one TypeScript module; Desktop's Rust code reads a generated mirror.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds every model fact in JSON under packages/ai/model-registry/catalog, compiles it into a registry plus models.json, and exposes lookups (alias to canonical id, provider display, routes, capabilities, tier access, lifecycle) through packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:37, :54, :57; packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1446).
purpose.why_it_exists: So no surface keeps its own copy of model ids, prices, capabilities or plan limits, and a model swap never needs a consumer edit (doc: AGENTS.md section 4; packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1-18).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and operators edit and sync it. Every app and the server read it. End users see only the result: the models in the picker, plan locks, and retirement notices.
problems_solved: Duplicated model lists drifting between apps and server.
A model id typo or retired id reaching a provider.
Plan limits defined in more than one place.
Unknown lifecycle state: whether a model is new, old, or being retired.
use_cases: A developer adds a model to the curation file, runs sync, and every picker shows it.
A model is marked deprecated with a date; routing then refuses to pick it once the date has passed.
A client sends a provider API model id or an old alias; the catalog resolves it to the canonical id.
The server checks which plan a model needs and names it in an error.

where_to_find_it: No screen edits the catalog. Web: the model trigger in the chat composer footer opens the picker built from it (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx:1932, packages/ai/routing/src/model-picker.ts:272).
Chrome extension: managed model picker (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedModelPicker.ts, uses buildModelPickerShortList per grep).
Desktop (public Electron app) shows the hosted web app, so it shows the web picker (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
prerequisites: Developer side: pnpm and the repo. Edit packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/models.curation.json, then run pnpm sync:models (package.json:386).
User side: none for seeing the picker; plan decides which rows are locked.
screens_and_controls: Picker rows show name, plan lock label, release stage label (preview, experimental, beta, alpha) (packages/ai/routing/src/model-picker.ts:195, :247).
Mobile shows 'Retires <date>' when a model retires within 30 days (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/retirement.ts:7, :18).
Mobile shows a notice that a retired model used by a chat has been retired and names the replacement if one is recorded (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/retirement.ts:30).
journey: Developer edits catalog/models.curation.json or another catalog file.
Developer runs pnpm sync:models; compile.mjs validates against a schema and writes registry.json, registry.ts, models.json and the Rust mirror (scripts/compile.mjs:37-57).
pnpm sync:models:check and pnpm check:model-catalog fail CI if generated files or integrity drift (package.json:387, :361).
Surfaces read the new data; the person opens the picker and sees the model, locked or open by plan.
A retired id in an old chat resolves to a name through the retirement record, so old messages still show a name (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1504).
feedback_and_outputs: Plan lock labels and release-stage labels in the picker.
Retirement label and retired-model notice on Mobile.

unknown: the exact wording of web or desktop retirement notices; a search of apps/web found no consumer of the retirement record (grep for getRetiredModelMetadataById in apps/web/app and apps/web/lib found none; apps/web/features not searched).
settings: None for the person. Operator tools: pnpm sync:models, sync:models:check, sync:models:refresh, models:families (package.json:386-394).

working: Compiler reads catalog JSON, validates it and writes generated registry and models.json (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:37-57, :3145).
Alias resolution: canonical ids, provider api model ids and per-provider canonicalization map to one canonical id (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1427-1452).
Provider registry: provider labels, display ids, aliases, default model, surface (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1609-1664).
Route registry: one record per provider and model with harness, trust modes, response formats and commercial status (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:143-157).
Capability registry splits intrinsic and route-dependent capability names (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:190-195).
Plan tiers: TIER_POLICIES per free, pro, max, enterprise with allowed slots and allowed provider surfaces (managed_cloud, byok, local) (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1065, :1413).

Lifecycle: 11 stages from discovered to removed, with named shortcuts (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/lifecycle-stages.mjs:12-49); deprecation date check (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1181); retired records keep identity and replacement (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1469-1500).

Routing enforces lifecycle: a deprecated model, or one past its deprecation date, is not eligible (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1356-1358); the server passes the past-date set into every managed routing request (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/routing-request.ts:109).
Which generation of a model family is live is owned by model-families.json; promote or roll back with models:families scripts (doc: AGENTS.md section 4; package.json:394-396).
incomplete: Successor handling is a notice only. A pinned retired or deprecated model is refused, not swapped for its replacement (packages/ai/routing/src/__tests__/retired-model-selection.test.ts:23-30). The replacement is shown only on Mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/retirement.ts:30); web and other apps: unknown.

Brief item S91.06 says lifecycle is 'enforced'; the code enforces eligibility in routing, but the stage value itself is only recorded in the registry. Whether any consumer other than the compiler and tools reads the stage: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Brief line numbers for S91.01 (model-catalog.ts:1367) and S91.05 (:1340) no longer match; the code is at :1121 and :1427-1446. The brief is stale on this point.
not_available: Batch or deferred inference is a separate brief item (S91.30), outside this feature.
Own-key (BYOK) and local trust modes are in the catalog (harness trust modes), but the compiled route data is shared; whether each app uses them: see F091-02 and unknowns.

established.statement: One compiled model registry is the source every surface and the server read for model facts.
A provider registry records each provider (display, defaults, governance, hosts).
A provider-route registry records every model x provider route with harness, trust modes, retention, cache class and price.
A capability registry records intrinsic and route-dependent capabilities per model.
Model aliases resolve to canonical model ids everywhere.
Model lifecycle (stage, deprecation, retirement, replacement) is managed and enforced.
The model catalog is generated and is the only place a model id may be a literal; never hand-edit models.json.
AGI never claims a model or provider can do something if capability metadata does not prove it.

acceptance_criteria: After editing the curation file and running pnpm sync:models, pnpm sync:models:check passes and models.json changed only through the generator.
Resolving a provider api model id, an alias and a canonical id returns the same canonical id.
A model whose deprecation date is in the past is not selected by Auto and is refused when pinned, on every plan and trust mode.
The picker shows a plan lock for a model the plan does not include, using the tier policy from the catalog.
A message stored with a retired model id still shows a model name.
An inline model id literal in app code fails pnpm check:model-id-literals.
inferred: [inferred] The picker hides or locks models by the same tier policy the server uses, because both read model-catalog.ts.
[inferred] A retired model should show a successor on every app, as Mobile does; only Mobile is evidenced.
proposed: [proposed] Show the retirement notice and replacement on web and extensions, the way Mobile does.
[proposed] Add a test that every surface picker reads the retirement label from one shared helper.

steps.what_happens: Developer edits catalog JSON and runs the sync command.
Compiler validates the catalog and writes registry.json, registry.ts, models.json and the Rust mirror files.
Apps import the compiled data at build time; the server and routing package read the same registry in process.
At request time the server resolves the incoming model id to the canonical id and reads tier, routes and lifecycle from it.
Picker rows are built from the same catalog on the person's device, with plan locks from the tier policy.

data.what: Catalog source JSON and generated registry and models.json
data.where_stored: Repository files under packages/ai/model-registry and packages/contracts/types/src
data.synced: Shipped inside each app build and the server build; no runtime sync found.
data.retained_or_deleted: Kept in git; retired models stay as records in retired-models.json (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:45).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The catalog describes every provider route (managed cloud, own key, local harnesses) but does not call any provider itself; compile.mjs may refresh synced data from outside sources only in its refresh mode (packages/ai/model-registry/package.json scripts: refresh).

access_and_usage.account: Reading the catalog needs no account. Account matters only when a request is made: the server checks the plan (apps/web/lib/model-tiers.ts:9).
access_and_usage.permissions: Editing needs repository write access; CI guards block drift (package.json:361, :387).
access_and_usage.subscription: TIER_POLICIES define allowed slots, manual selection, caps per tier free, pro, max, enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1065, :1413). Minimum plan for a model: getMinimumRequiredTier (:2196). The brief says plan limits come from this catalog; plan display names come from the billing catalog, not read here.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Price per route and token caps per tier live in the catalog (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1413 for tokenCapPerMonth); metering itself is another feature.
access_and_usage.flags: Family promotion via models:families scripts (package.json:394-396). No runtime feature flag found for the catalog itself.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Capabilities are recorded per model and per route; routes decide route-dependent ones (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:190-195).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Each route carries trust modes (managed_cloud, byok, local) and each provider has governance data (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1066, :143-152).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Tier policies list 'local' as an allowed provider surface on the max and enterprise tiers I opened (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1356, :1394); the mobile local picker offers Auto on every plan because on-device routing costs nothing (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/ModelPickerSheet.tsx:316-325). On-device model files are described separately in on-device-models.ts. Whether the free tier lists the local surface: not read, unknown.

states_and_edge_cases.behaviour: getModelMetadataById returns null; the router returns code unknown_selection; the chat endpoint answers 422 model_route_unavailable.
Name is still resolvable for old messages; pinned selection is refused, never swapped.
Model drops out of routing even if still marked active.
Catalog is bundled data, so it needs no network; not applicable.
Web picker trigger has an aria-label naming the model and 'Change model'.

corrections.claim: Tier policies list 'local' as an allowed surface on max and enterprise tiers (model-catalog.ts:1356, :1394); whether the free tier lists local: unknown.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Facts right, citations wrong. max allows ['managed_cloud','byok','local'] at :1329; enterprise at :1380. Lines 1356 and 1394 are not those lines (:1356 is inside the enterprise block, :1394 is tokenCapPerMonth: null). The 'unknown' is answerable: free is ['managed_cloud'] only (:1245); pro is ['managed_cloud','byok'] (:1281).
corrections.correction: Local surface is allowed only on max (:1329) and enterprise (:1380). Free is managed_cloud only (:1245). Pro is managed_cloud and byok (:1281).

corrections.claim: Token caps per tier live in the catalog (model-catalog.ts:1413 for tokenCapPerMonth).
corrections.what_the_code_shows: :1413 is `export const TIER_POLICIES = TIER_POLICIES_DEFINITION`. The caps are at :1257 (free null), :1295 (pro 40,000,000), :1347 (max 100,000,000), :1394 (enterprise null).
corrections.correction: Token caps per month are in TIER_POLICIES: free null, pro 40M, max 100M, enterprise null (:1257, :1295, :1347, :1394).

corrections.claim: TIER_POLICIES cover free, pro, max, enterprise; plan ids in code are free, basic, pro, max, enterprise.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: ProductTier is 'free'|'pro'|'max'|'enterprise' (:1065), with no 'basic' policy. But getMinimumRequiredTier returns 'free'|'basic'|'pro'|'max' (:2196) and returns 'basic' for economy models not named free. The page never says that a 'basic' floor exists with no TIER_POLICIES entry, and that canAccessModelForSubscriptionTier decides it separately.
corrections.correction: Tier policies exist for four tiers. The minimum-plan lookup works on a different set that includes 'basic' (:2196).

missing_facts: Free tier allowedProviderSurfaces is ['managed_cloud'] only and pro is ['managed_cloud','byok']. Local is limited to max and enterprise, and BYOK needs pro or above. The page leaves this as 'unknown' (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1245, :1281, :1329, :1380).
Token caps differ by tier. The page never states them: free null, pro 40M, max 100M, enterprise null (model-catalog.ts:1257, :1295, :1347, :1394).

The routing 'on_device' trust mode exists beside managed_cloud, byok and local, and the retired-model test covers it (packages/ai/routing/src/__tests__/retired-model-selection.test.ts:17). The page's trust-mode lists omit it.
